topic: The Visual Language of Matrices: Geometric Intuition in Linear Algebra
target_audience: First-year university students or STEM-focused high school students

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Vector as a Path
lecture_lines: Imagine a vector as a path from the origin.
Meet i-hat and j-hat, our grid's unit steps.
Every vector is a combination of these steps.
animations: Create a dark grid #222222 with the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg] icon at the origin (0, 0).
Draw a blue arrow #58C4DD (i-hat) and a red arrow #FC6255 (j-hat) starting from the origin.
Draw a green vector #83C167 pointing to (3, 2) as the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg] icon moves from (0,0) to (3,2).

sections.title: The Concept of Linear Transformation
lecture_lines: A linear transformation warps the space around us.
The origin remains fixed throughout the transformation.
Grid lines stay parallel and evenly spaced.
animations: Animate the grid lines #444444 warping into a shear transformation where vertical lines tilt.
Highlight the origin (0, 0) with a white #FFFFFF dot [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/null.svg] to show it remains fixed.
Flash parallel grid lines #AAFFCC to demonstrate they remain straight and evenly spaced.

sections.title: The Matrix as a 'Landing Map'
lecture_lines: We only track where the basis vectors land.
Watch i-hat and j-hat move to their new spots.
The matrix records these two landing positions.
The first column shows where i-hat landed.
The second column tracks the destination of j-hat.
animations: Draw unit vectors i-hat #58C4DD and j-hat #FC6255 on a standard coordinate grid.
Transform the grid so i-hat moves to [1, 1] and j-hat moves to [-2, 0].
Display a 2x2 matrix [[1, -2], [1, 0]] in white #FFFFFF at the top of the screen.
Highlight the first matrix column #58C4DD and pulse the transformed i-hat vector.
Highlight the second matrix column #FC6255 and pulse the transformed j-hat vector.

sections.title: Visualizing Matrix-Vector Multiplication
lecture_lines: Matrix multiplication scales these new basis vectors.
Follow three units of our transformed i-hat vector.
Then add two units of the new j-hat.
Pixel arrives at the final transformed position.
The formula combines these scaled basis vectors.
animations: Display the transformed i-hat #58C4DD and j-hat #FC6255 vectors from the previous section.
Show three copies of the transformed i-hat vector placed end-to-end from the origin.
Attach two copies of the transformed j-hat vector to the end of the i-hat chain.
Animate the Pixel icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pixel.svg] sliding from the origin along this combined vector path.
Display the color-coded vector addition formula '3*i_new + 2*j_new' matching the arrows.

sections.title: The Determinant: The Scaling Factor
lecture_lines: The determinant measures how much areas change.
This unit rug stretches as the grid warps.
Its new area represents the matrix determinant.
A determinant of three means the area tripled.
If it is zero, the area completely collapses.
animations: Highlight a 1x1 yellow square #FFFF00 'rug' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rug.svg] with corners at (0,0) and (1,1).
Animate the grid transformation, stretching the yellow square into a parallelogram.
Fill the parallelogram with orange #FFA500 and show the area value '3' inside it.
Display the text 'Determinant = 3' in white #FFFFFF next to the transformed rug [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rug.svg].
Animate the grid collapsing into a single line, showing the determinant reaching 0.

sections.title: Summary & Intuition Check
lecture_lines: Matrices move basis vectors to transform our world.
Visualizing this makes linear algebra feel intuitive.
Master the visual language of matrices.
animations: Show row of white #FFFFFF icons/text for 'Vector', 'Matrix', and 'Determinant'.
Play a rapid montage of three different linear transformations with Pixel reacting.
Fade everything to the final title 'The Visual Language of Matrices' in white #FFFFFF.
